sections.h2: Where is Hilton Head Island, and what makes the island different from a mainland city?
sections.html:
Hilton Head Island is a barrier island in Beaufort County, in the South Carolina Lowcountry, about 20 miles northeast of Savannah, Georgia. Everything about a sale here is shaped by the fact that it is an island: the bridge, the tides, the gates and the water.

The Town's total area is 69.13 square miles, but only 41.35 of that is land. The island is shaped like a shoe, with about 12 miles of Atlantic beachfront, and Broad Creek separates an older northern section from a younger southern one. Soils outside the tidal marsh are sandy.

About 70% of the island, including most of the resort areas, lies inside gated communities. Sea Pines Resort, Hilton Head Plantation, Palmetto Dunes, Shipyard Plantation and Port Royal Plantation are the best known. Each has its own association and rules, so an owner inside one needs to learn those rules before any sale.

sections.h2: What is the history of Hilton Head Island in brief?
sections.html:
The island is named for Captain William Hilton, who identified a headland near Port Royal Sound in 1663. Native Americans lived there for thousands of years before that, and Spanish explorers arrived in 1521.

Confederate Fort Walker fell to more than 12,000 Union troops on November 7, 1861, and the island became a major base for the blockade of Southern ports. Hundreds of freed people settled there during the war, and many of their Gullah descendants still live on the island.

Modern development began in the 1950s. The James F. Byrnes Bridge opened in 1956, the same year Charles E. Fraser started Sea Pines. A four lane bridge replaced the old swing bridge in 1982, Cross Island Parkway opened in January 1997, and the Town was incorporated after a May 1983 referendum.

sections.h2: What drives the Hilton Head Island economy?
sections.html:
Tourism drives the economy. About 2.5 million visitors come each year, and the population can reach roughly 150,000 in peak summer. Golf is a major draw: the RBC Heritage, a PGA Tour event, is played at Harbour Town Golf Links in Sea Pines.

The top employers listed in the Town's 2021 financial report show the pattern:

  • SERG Group Restaurants, 1,244 employees
  • Marriott Vacation Club, 580
  • Sea Pines Resort, 536
  • Hilton Head Medical Center and Clinics, 506

Hilton Head Airport is owned by Beaufort County and has service from American, Delta and United. The main road from the mainland is William Hilton Parkway. Many homes here are second homes or rentals, so a seller often lives elsewhere and needs a sale that does not require flying in for open houses.

sections.h2: How do flood zones and weather affect a Hilton Head Island house?
sections.html:
Flood zone status is part of nearly every Hilton Head Island sale. The climate is humid subtropical, with a July average high of 90 degrees, a January average low of 38 degrees and about 51.4 inches of rain a year. August is the wettest month at 8.9 inches.

The Town publishes a Flood Hazard Zone Search. Its guide lists Zone X (low risk), shaded Zone X (0.2% annual chance), Zone AE and Zone VE (1% annual chance, with wave action in VE) and Zone AO (shallow flooding). The Town says it is a Class 5 community in FEMA's Community Rating System and has participated since 1991, which it says gives property owners a 25% discount on flood insurance premiums.

If you plan to sell, gather these records first:

  • A current elevation certificate, which the Floodplain Administrator can help with
  • Building permit history, which the Town lets you search by address
  • Your flood insurance declarations page

The Town's records page says permits for buildings from after April 2014, from 1984 to April 2014, and from before 1984 each sit in a different system, with the oldest requested from Beaufort County. Call the Floodplain Administrator at 843-341-4600 with zone questions.

sections.h2: What are the short-term rental rules on Hilton Head Island?
sections.html:
A house used for vacation rentals needs a Town permit and a business license, and the rules are strict enough to affect a sale. The Town says the permit is issued to an individual, not to a business entity, and the permit number must appear in every advertisement.

Other requirements listed by the Town include an HOA approval letter where one applies, a site plan showing trash and parking, a reachable owner or agent during each rental with a one hour complaint response, and the 3% Local Accommodations Tax. Houses of 3,600 square feet or more need a fire suppression or approved monitoring system, and bedrooms must meet code and be primarily for sleeping.

The Town's pages do not say what happens to a permit when the house sells. Ask the STR office at 843-341-4740 or STRPlan@hiltonheadislandsc.gov before you tell a buyer the rental income comes with the house.

sections.h2: How do Beaufort County property taxes work for a Hilton Head Island owner?
sections.html:
Hilton Head Island owners pay property tax to Beaufort County, and the difference between the 4% and 6% assessment ratio can be large. South Carolina assesses an owner-occupied legal residence at 4% and other real property, including second homes, at 6%.

Beaufort County's application for the 4% rate is due by January 15, and taxes are due by that date whether or not the application is approved. Renting the home for more than 72 days in a calendar year, moving your legal residence or selling the property must be reported to the Assessor within six months. The penalty for keeping the 4% rate improperly is 100% of the tax paid plus 0.5% interest per month, with a $30 minimum. A new owner must submit a fresh application.

State law makes taxes due between September 30 and January 15, with a 3% penalty after January 15, 7% more after February 1 and 5% more after March 16. Counties may offer installments under Section 12-45-75, but we did not confirm that Beaufort County does, so ask the Treasurer.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed in Beaufort County involve?
sections.html:
Deeds for Hilton Head Island go to the Beaufort County Register of Deeds at 100 Ribaut Road in Beaufort, open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays. The county lists a $15 flat fee for a deed plus $1.85 per $500 of consideration, as of August 1, 2019, and a 0.25% Hilton Head Island transfer fee in certain district numbers.

The county also requires original signatures, two witnesses, a notary statement, the District Map Parcel number, the buyer's address and a derivation clause. An Affidavit of True Consideration is needed when the deed does not state the price on its face. E-recording partners include Simplifile and CSC Global, and documents received after 4:30 p.m. are processed the next business day.

Confirm current fees with the office, because the posted schedule carries a 2019 date.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work on Hilton Head Island?
sections.html:
A cash sale lets an island owner skip the showings, the lender appraisal and the wait for a buyer who can qualify for a mortgage. We look at the property as it is, including any flood, roof or HOA issues, and you pick a closing date.

Inherited homes, vacant second homes and houses with deferred maintenance are common here. We make no promise on price before reviewing the house, and you can turn the offer down at no cost.

faqs.q: Is Hilton Head Island its own town?
faqs.a: Yes. The Town of Hilton Head Island was incorporated after a May 1983 referendum. It sits in Beaufort County, which handles assessments, tax bills and deed recording.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hilton Head Island house inside a gated community?
faqs.a: Yes. About 70% of the island lies inside gated communities, and each has an association with its own rules. Ask the association what a sale requires, such as notices or fees.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the 4% and 6% tax rate in Beaufort County?
faqs.a: The 4% ratio applies to a legal residence the owner lives in. Second homes and other real property are assessed at 6%. The legal residence application is due January 15, and a new owner must apply again.

faqs.q: Does my short-term rental permit transfer to a buyer?
faqs.a: The Town's pages do not say. The permit is issued to an individual, so contact the STR office at 843-341-4740 before you promise anything to a buyer.

faqs.q: What flood records should I have ready to sell?
faqs.a: Have an elevation certificate, your flood zone from the Town's search tool and your permit history. The Town's Floodplain Administrator can help with certificates.

faqs.q: How much is the deed recording fee in Beaufort County?
faqs.a: The county posts $15 plus $1.85 per $500 of consideration, as of August 1, 2019, and a 0.25% transfer fee in certain districts on Hilton Head Island. Check with the Register of Deeds for current amounts.
